title: Counting chromosomes: aneuploidy
caption: A typical human cell has 46 chromosomes: 44 autosomes and two sex chromosomes. Non-disjunction gives gametes with an extra or a missing chromosome, so the offspring have, for example, three copies of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21, Down syndrome, 47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21), only one sex chromosome (Turner syndrome, 45,X) or an extra X (Klinefelter syndrome, 47,XXY). Aneuploidy is an abnormal number of one chromosome.
alt: Four rows. Typical: two copies of chromosome 21 and either XX or XY, 46 chromosomes. Down syndrome: three copies of chromosome 21, 47. Turner syndrome: a single X, 45. Klinefelter syndrome: XXY, 47.
description: Down syndrome: trisomy 21, three copies of chromosome 21: 47,XX,+21.
Aneuploidy is an abnormal number of one chromosome; non-disjunction in meiosis is its usual cause.
